name: Citalopram

binding.notes: Racemate; S-enantiomer carries activity. Hyttel JCP 1994 reports Ki ~1-4 nM for citalopram across multiple preparations.
Highest off-target among citalopram receptors; underlies sedation.
Weakest sigma-1 affinity among SSRIs aside from paroxetine.

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Acute SERT blockade raises synaptic 5-HT; chronic dosing produces somatodendritic 5-HT1A autoreceptor desensitisation (delayed onset of antidepressant effect).

neuroimaging.finding: 20 mg/day citalopram produces ~80% striatal SERT occupancy measured by [11C]-DASB; occupancy plateaus above 40 mg/day.

drug_interactions_pk.clinical_effect: Citalopram AUC ↑ ~40%; pushes plasma into QTc-risk range at >20mg.

pharmacogenetics.phenotype_effects: CYP2C19 PMs show 2-3× citalopram AUC and elevated QTc; CPIC recommends max 20 mg/day for PMs. UMs may have subtherapeutic exposure. 5-HTTLPR S-allele homozygotes show worse response.

tolerance_and_dependence.receptor_downregulation_half_time: 5-HT1A autoreceptor desensitisation 2-3 weeks in humans (PET evidence)
tolerance_and_dependence.withdrawal_syndrome: SSRI discontinuation syndrome — flu-like symptoms, dizziness, paresthesias ('brain zaps'), anxiety; onset 2-3 days, peak 5-7 days, duration 1-3 weeks. Less severe than paroxetine due to longer t1/2.

off_targets.clinical_consequence: QTc prolongation, torsade de pointes; FDA black-box restriction limits dose to 40 mg (20 mg in elderly/CYP2C19 PMs).
DDCT/DCT metabolite shows greater hERG potency than parent; contributes to QTc effect.

demographic_differences.age: Elderly: clearance ↓ ~30%; FDA limits dose to 20 mg in ≥60 years.
demographic_differences.renal_or_hepatic: Hepatic impairment: clearance ↓ ~37%, t1/2 doubles. Dose limit 20 mg/day.

notes: Racemate; R-enantiomer is pharmacologically inactive at SERT but contributes to hERG affinity and antagonises the active S-enantiomer via allosteric site (basis for escitalopram development).

name: Escitalopram

binding.notes: S-enantiomer carries SERT activity; ~30-fold more potent than R-citalopram.
Allosteric site in TM10-12 (residues A505/L506/I507/S574/I575); binding here slows escitalopram dissociation from orthosteric site, enhancing inhibition. Mechanism unique to citalopram series.
6× lower H1 affinity than racemic citalopram (the R-enantiomer contributes the H1 binding).

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Same as citalopram (SERT blockade → synaptic 5-HT rise). Allosteric self-potentiation produces a steeper occupancy-dose curve than the racemate.

neuroimaging.finding: 10 mg/day escitalopram produces ~80% SERT occupancy (similar to 40 mg citalopram).

drug_interactions_pk.clinical_effect: Escitalopram AUC ↑ ~50%; clinically modest QTc effect compared to racemic citalopram.

pharmacogenetics.phenotype_effects: CYP2C19 PMs show ~2× AUC; CPIC recommends 50% dose reduction. UMs show ~40% lower AUC. Less QTc concern than racemic citalopram because R-enantiomer (which contributes to hERG block) is absent.

tolerance_and_dependence.withdrawal_syndrome: SSRI discontinuation syndrome — generally milder than paroxetine, similar to citalopram.

off_targets.clinical_consequence: Lower QTc effect than racemic citalopram (R-citalopram is the primary hERG blocker in racemate).

demographic_differences.age: Elderly: AUC ~50% higher; consider 5-10 mg/day starting dose.
demographic_differences.renal_or_hepatic: Hepatic impairment: half clearance, double t1/2.

notes: Therapeutic exploitation of citalopram's SERT allosteric site is the canonical example of allosteric self-potentiation in clinical psychopharmacology.

name: Fluoxetine

binding.notes: Tatsumi et al. 1997 — definitive monoamine transporter Ki table for antidepressants.
Competitive reversible 5-HT2C antagonism is functionally relevant — disinhibits prefrontal DA/NE release.

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: SERT blockade plus 5-HT2C antagonism produces secondary disinhibition of frontal cortex DA/NE — accounts for activating profile distinct from other SSRIs.

routes.notes: Parent t1/2 1-3 days acute; 4-6 days chronic. Norfluoxetine t1/2 ~7-15 days (essentially eliminates need for tapering).

drug_interactions_pk.clinical_effect: Strong CYP2D6 inhibition persists 4-6 weeks after stopping due to long t1/2. Reduces tamoxifen → endoxifen conversion; phenocopies CYP2D6 PM.
Moderate inhibitor; raises levels of midazolam, alprazolam.

pharmacogenetics.phenotype_effects: CYP2D6 PMs: fluoxetine AUC ↑, norfluoxetine AUC ↓. Because norfluoxetine has comparable SERT potency to parent and longer t1/2, total active drug exposure is similar across phenotypes — fluoxetine is unusually robust to CYP2D6 polymorphism.

tolerance_and_dependence.withdrawal_syndrome: Mildest discontinuation among SSRIs because norfluoxetine self-tapers over weeks. Rarely requires dose taper.

off_targets.clinical_consequence: Minimal QTc effect at therapeutic doses.

demographic_differences.age: Pediatric (8-18y): faster clearance — same mg/kg dosing achievable. Elderly: clearance unchanged but t1/2 prolonged due to comorbidity.
demographic_differences.renal_or_hepatic: Hepatic impairment: t1/2 doubles; halve dose.

notes: The long half-life of norfluoxetine (~7-15 days) makes fluoxetine the SSRI most likely to cause serotonin syndrome when switching to MAOIs (requires 5-week washout) and most robust to occasional missed doses.

name: Fluvoxamine

binding.notes: Highest sigma-1 affinity in the SSRI class; fluvoxamine is the prototypical sigma-1 agonist among prescribed antidepressants. Sigma-1 agonism implicated in pro-cognitive and ER-stress-attenuating effects.

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Sigma-1 agonism translocates the chaperone from ER mitochondria-associated membranes to plasma membrane, modulating IP3 receptor Ca2+ release and ER stress response.

drug_interactions_pk.clinical_effect: Clozapine AUC ↑ 5-10×; can produce severe sedation/agranulocytosis risk. Sometimes used deliberately to lower clozapine dose requirements.
Theophylline clearance ↓ 60-70%; can cause toxicity at standard theophylline doses.
Tizanidine AUC ↑ 33×, Cmax ↑ 12×; severe hypotension/sedation. Contraindicated combination.
Caffeine half-life roughly 5×; clinically meaningful insomnia/anxiety.

pharmacogenetics.phenotype_effects: CYP2D6 PMs show higher fluvoxamine exposure but clinical impact is less than for fluoxetine/paroxetine.

tolerance_and_dependence.withdrawal_syndrome: Shortest t1/2 SSRI besides paroxetine → discontinuation syndrome onset within 1-3 days, can be severe.

off_targets.clinical_consequence: Plasma melatonin levels ↑ 17× due to CYP1A2 inhibition of melatonin metabolism.

demographic_differences.age: Elderly: t1/2 ~17-26 h vs 13-16 h in younger adults.

notes: Strongest CYP1A2 inhibitor among SSRIs — clinically defining interaction profile.

name: Paroxetine

binding.notes: Highest SERT affinity of any approved SSRI. Crystal structure of paroxetine-hSERT complex resolved (Coleman et al. 2020).
Highest NET affinity of any SSRI — paroxetine functions as a weak SNRI at higher doses.
Most anticholinergic SSRI — accounts for dry mouth, constipation, cognitive blunting.
Lowest sigma-1 affinity of any SSRI.
Novel NOS inhibition (Finkel et al. 1996) — paroxetine is unique among SSRIs in this property; implicated in sexual dysfunction profile.

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: SERT blockade plus NOS inhibition; NOS inhibition contributes to nitric-oxide-mediated penile/vaginal vasodilation impairment, hence the highest rate of sexual dysfunction among SSRIs.

drug_interactions_pk.clinical_effect: Strongest clinical CYP2D6 inhibitor. Phenocopies CYP2D6 PM. Tamoxifen→endoxifen reduced; codeine→morphine analgesia abolished.

pharmacogenetics.phenotype_effects: CYP2D6 PMs show ~3-7× higher plasma paroxetine. Paradoxically, autoinhibition of CYP2D6 makes EMs behave like PMs at steady state — major source of nonlinear PK.

tolerance_and_dependence.withdrawal_syndrome: Worst SSRI discontinuation syndrome — short t1/2 plus muscarinic rebound. Onset within 24 h, peak day 3-5, may persist 2-4 weeks. 'Brain zaps,' dizziness, vivid dreams, irritability classic.

demographic_differences.renal_or_hepatic: Severe renal/hepatic impairment: Cmax ↑ 2-7×; start at 10 mg/day.

notes: Pregnancy category D for first-trimester cardiac malformation risk — only SSRI with this designation.

binding.notes: Sertraline is the only SSRI with clinically meaningful DAT affinity (~50× lower than SERT but still 10× higher than other SSRIs). Likely contributes to its activating profile and abuse-deterrent characteristics.
Sertraline acts as a sigma-1 inverse agonist (unlike fluvoxamine which is an agonist). Inhibits NGF-induced neurite outgrowth via sigma-1, suppresses hippocampal LTP at low μM.

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: SERT + DAT + sigma-1 inverse agonism. The DAT component may give sertraline a mild stimulant edge over other SSRIs but is not high enough for abuse liability.

drug_interactions_pk.clinical_effect: Weak-moderate CYP2D6 inhibitor; clinically less significant than paroxetine or fluoxetine.

pharmacogenetics.phenotype_effects: CYP2C19 PMs and CYP2B6 *6/*6 carriers show ~50% higher AUC. CPIC recommends 50% dose reduction in CYP2C19 PMs.

tolerance_and_dependence.withdrawal_syndrome: Moderate — between fluoxetine (mild) and paroxetine (severe). Onset 1-3 days; peak 3-5 days.

off_targets.clinical_consequence: Mild activating effect; suggested but not proven to confer modest weight benefit vs other SSRIs.

demographic_differences.sex: Women have ~30% higher AUC at fixed dose.

name: Mirtazapine

binding.notes: Among the most potent H1 antagonists in clinical use — accounts for sedation, weight gain, appetite stimulation.
5-HT3 antagonism gives anti-nausea property and avoids GI side-effects typical of SSRIs.
Central α2 autoreceptor antagonism on noradrenergic neurons disinhibits NE release; heteroreceptor blockade on serotonergic terminals enhances 5-HT release. Core 'NaSSA' mechanism.
Weak muscarinic affinity → minimal anticholinergic effects.
Mirtazapine has negligible SERT/NET binding — does not directly inhibit reuptake.

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: α2 antagonism increases NE release; NE acts on serotonergic cell bodies α1 to increase 5-HT cell firing; 5-HT2A/2C/3 blockade channels the released 5-HT specifically to 5-HT1A. The 'noradrenergic and specific serotonergic antidepressant' (NaSSA) mechanism.

drug_interactions_pk.clinical_effect: Mirtazapine AUC ↑ 50%, Cmax ↑ 40%.

pharmacogenetics.phenotype_effects: CYP2D6 PMs show modestly higher mirtazapine exposure; clinically minor.

tolerance_and_dependence.receptor_downregulation_half_time: H1 sedation tolerance develops within 1-2 weeks (paradoxically: 15 mg more sedating than 30 mg because α2 antagonism — which is alerting via NE release — emerges at higher doses)
tolerance_and_dependence.withdrawal_syndrome: Generally mild; flu-like symptoms, anxiety, insomnia possible. Onset 1-3 days, duration 1-2 weeks.

demographic_differences.sex: Women have ~25% higher AUC than men.

notes: Dose-dependent sedation paradox: 15 mg is more sedating than 30 mg because at higher doses α2-mediated noradrenergic alerting offsets H1-mediated sedation. Frequent off-label use as a sleep aid uses the low end.

name: Olanzapine

binding.notes: Bymaster et al. 1996 — definitive olanzapine receptor profile.
5-HT2A:D2 ratio of ~3:1 is the canonical 'atypical' fingerprint.
5-HT2C antagonism is a key driver of olanzapine-induced weight gain and metabolic syndrome.
Major contributor to sedation and weight gain.
Strong M1 antagonism. Anticholinergic effects, but also protects against EPS.
M3 antagonism on pancreatic β-cells implicated in insulin secretion impairment and type 2 diabetes risk.
Orthostatic hypotension.

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: 5-HT2A antagonism enhances frontal-cortex DA release while D2 blockade reduces mesolimbic DA — the classic 'atypical' separation of antipsychotic from EPS effect.

neuroimaging.finding: 10 mg/day olanzapine produces ~63% striatal D2 occupancy ([11C]-raclopride) and >85% 5-HT2A occupancy ([18F]-setoperone). 20 mg/day pushes D2 to ~80%, above which EPS risk rises sharply.
M2 muscarinic occupancy in patients on therapeutic doses ~40-60% ([123I]-IQNB).

drug_interactions_pk.clinical_effect: Olanzapine AUC ↑ ~2×; dose reduction recommended.
Smokers require ~30-40% higher dose; abrupt smoking cessation → toxicity risk.
Olanzapine AUC ↓ ~50%.

pharmacogenetics.phenotype_effects: CYP1A2*1F induction-prone allele plus smoking → significantly lower exposure. UGT1A4 polymorphisms have modest effect.

tolerance_and_dependence.receptor_downregulation_half_time: D2 supersensitivity may develop with chronic use → tardive dyskinesia risk (cumulative >1 year).
tolerance_and_dependence.withdrawal_syndrome: Cholinergic rebound (nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, insomnia) due to abrupt unmasking of muscarinic activity. Dyskinesia possible.

off_targets.clinical_consequence: Insulin secretion impairment → type 2 diabetes (independent of weight gain).

demographic_differences.sex: Women have ~30% lower clearance than men.

notes: Combines highest weight-gain liability among atypicals (H1 + 5-HT2C + M3) with potent antipsychotic efficacy approaching clozapine — the classic efficacy/metabolic trade-off.

name: Moclobemide

binding.notes: Reversible competitive MAO-A inhibitor (RIMA). Selectivity ratio MAO-A:MAO-B ~10:1 in vitro, higher in vivo because the reversibility means MAO-B remains available.

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Reversible MAO-A inhibition raises 5-HT, NE, and DA in synapses. Reversibility means tyramine displaces moclobemide from MAO-A, preserving substantial first-pass intestinal tyramine metabolism — accounts for far lower hypertensive crisis risk than irreversible MAOIs.

routes.subject_demographics: Healthy adults; bioavailability increases to ~90% after multiple doses due to autoinhibition

drug_interactions_pk.clinical_effect: Moclobemide AUC ↑ ~80% in CYP2C19 EMs; little effect in PMs (already saturated).
Moclobemide AUC ↑ ~2×.
Serotonin syndrome risk — combinations contraindicated despite reversibility.

pharmacogenetics.phenotype_effects: CYP2C19 PMs show ~2× higher AUC at single doses; converges after multiple dosing due to autoinhibition.

tolerance_and_dependence.withdrawal_syndrome: Mild; MAO-A activity restored within 24 h of discontinuation.

data_gaps_remaining: precise human MAO-A Ki under physiological conditions
notes: Reversibility is the defining feature — recommended washout to SSRI/MAOI switch is only 24-48 h vs 2 weeks for irreversible MAOIs.

name: Tranylcypromine

binding.notes: Irreversible covalent inhibitor — forms adduct with FAD cofactor via cyclopropyl ring opening. At low doses (20 mg/d) selective for MAO-A; at higher doses also inhibits MAO-B and gains weak DAT/NET inhibition.
Off-target epigenetic effect: lysine-specific demethylase 1 inhibition. Scaffold has been re-purposed for LSD1-inhibitor cancer drugs (e.g. iadademstat).

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Irreversible MAO inhibition causes accumulation of 5-HT, NE, DA, and phenethylamines. Trace amines (β-PEA, octopamine) accumulate and act as 'false neurotransmitters' on TAAR1.

drug_interactions_pk.mechanism: Pharmacodynamic — inability to deaminate dietary tyramine
drug_interactions_pk.clinical_effect: Hypertensive crisis. 'Cheese reaction' — defining safety issue.
Serotonin syndrome; contraindicated. 5-week washout from fluoxetine, 2 weeks from other SSRIs required.
Severe hypertension. Contraindicated.

tolerance_and_dependence.receptor_downregulation_half_time: MAO enzyme resynthesis ~2 weeks — pharmacodynamic effect outlasts plasma clearance by weeks
tolerance_and_dependence.withdrawal_syndrome: Possible flu-like syndrome, mood crash; rebound monoamine deficits.

off_targets.clinical_consequence: Epigenetic effect on H3K4 methylation; not directly therapeutic at antidepressant doses, but the scaffold inspired anti-cancer LSD1 inhibitor program.

demographic_differences.age: Elderly: ↑ hypertensive crisis risk, ↑ orthostatic hypotension.

data_gaps_remaining: precise in vivo Ki/Kinact for human MAO-A vs MAO-B
notes: Structurally amphetamine-like (cyclopropyl-locked phenethylamine), but amphetamine is NOT a metabolite (Baker et al. confirmed via mass spec). Has mild releasing activity in vitro.

name: phenelzine

binding.notes: Irreversible non-selective hydrazine MAO inhibitor; phenelzine is both substrate AND inhibitor — unusual.
Inhibition via the active metabolite β-phenylethylidenehydrazine (PEH). Raises brain GABA levels — contributes to anxiolytic effect distinct from monoamine actions.
Active metabolite raises brain alanine.

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Triple action: (1) irreversible MAO inhibition → 5-HT/NE/DA accumulation; (2) GABA-T inhibition → GABA accumulation (anxiolytic); (3) hydrazine moiety scavenges reactive aldehydes (acrolein, 4-HNE) — neuroprotective.

routes.subject_demographics: Healthy adults; phenelzine PK poorly characterised in humans because of its rapid clearance and the dominance of the irreversible PD effect.

drug_interactions_pk.clinical_effect: Hypertensive crisis — classic 'cheese reaction'.
Contraindicated; 2-5 week washout required.

pharmacogenetics.phenotype_effects: Slow N-acetylators (NAT2 PMs) may show altered phenelzine disposition; clinical significance uncertain.

tolerance_and_dependence.withdrawal_syndrome: Possible delirium, psychosis, rebound depression on abrupt discontinuation.

off_targets.clinical_consequence: Hydrazine moiety chelates pyridoxal phosphate; peripheral neuropathy if B6 depleted. Supplementation often recommended.

demographic_differences.renal_or_hepatic: Hepatotoxicity reported (hydrazine compounds historically liver-toxic); contraindicated in liver impairment.

data_gaps_remaining: quantitative human PK Cmax/Vd/AUC due to rapid metabolism and self-inactivation
notes: Unique among MAOIs in possessing GABAergic and aldehyde-scavenging activity via its active metabolite PEH. The 'no-human-data' tag in source is incorrect — phenelzine has 60+ years of human clinical use (Nardil).

name: Lithium orotate

binding.assay_buffer_notes: Mg2+ uncompetitive — Li+ binds the catalytic Mg2+ pocket
binding.notes: Direct Ki ~2 mM is above therapeutic serum lithium (0.6-1.2 mM) — but uncompetitive Mg-binding produces meaningful enzyme inhibition at clinical concentrations through enhanced Akt-mediated Ser9 phosphorylation.
Inositol depletion hypothesis: blocks PIP2 resynthesis → dampens 5-HT2/M1/α1 signalling.

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: GSK-3β inhibition stabilises β-catenin, raises Bcl-2/Mcl-1 (anti-apoptotic), inhibits Tau hyperphosphorylation. Inositol depletion modulates protein kinase C, suppresses cyclic 5-HT2/M1 signalling.

neuroimaging.finding: Chronic lithium increases brain N-acetylaspartate (neuronal viability marker) and gray-matter volume.

routes.subject_demographics: Lithium ion PK identical regardless of salt (orotate vs carbonate) per Smith 1976 in rats; human comparison not rigorously established. Orotate salt provides ~3.83 mg elemental Li per 100 mg.

metabolism.enzyme: none (lithium ion is renally excreted unchanged)

drug_interactions_pk.mechanism: Renal — reduced afferent arteriolar prostaglandin signalling reduces lithium clearance
drug_interactions_pk.clinical_effect: Lithium plasma ↑ ~25-50%; toxicity risk.

drug_interactions_pk.mechanism: Renal — increased proximal Na reabsorption increases Li retention
drug_interactions_pk.clinical_effect: Lithium ↑ ~25%.
Lithium ↑ 25-40%.

pharmacogenetics.phenotype_effects: GADL1 polymorphism associated with lithium response in Han Chinese (Chen 2014). Generally weak pharmacogenetic signal.

tolerance_and_dependence.receptor_downregulation_half_time: GSK-3 inhibition reaches steady-state over days-weeks
tolerance_and_dependence.withdrawal_syndrome: Discontinuation-related relapse risk (especially manic rebound in bipolar) — gradual taper recommended.

off_targets.clinical_consequence: Hypothyroidism in 5-35% of chronic users; goiter possible.
Nephrogenic diabetes insipidus (impairs vasopressin signalling); chronic kidney disease with long-term use.

demographic_differences.renal_or_hepatic: Renal impairment: avoid or significantly reduce. Hepatic impairment: no effect (no hepatic metabolism).

data_gaps_remaining: rigorous human PK comparison of orotate vs carbonate salt
evidence that lithium orotate at supplement doses (5-20 mg elemental) reaches clinically meaningful brain concentrations
notes: Lithium orotate provides ~3.83 mg elemental Li per 100 mg salt vs 18.8 mg from lithium carbonate. Supplement doses (typically 5-20 mg elemental) yield serum lithium typically <0.05 mM — well below the 0.6-1.2 mM therapeutic range for bipolar disorder. Hahnemann's 1976 study found no PK difference between salts; recent Smith/Schrauzer claims of preferential brain uptake of orotate salt are unsubstantiated in controlled studies.

name: Lamotrigine

binding.assay_buffer_notes: IC50 strongly voltage-dependent: 280 μM at -120 mV holding potential, 28.8 μM at -95 mV — use-dependent block of inactivated channels
binding.notes: Use-dependent / state-dependent — preferentially binds inactivated state. Stabilises Na channel inactivation, reduces glutamate/aspartate release.
Cardiac Na channel block underlies FDA warning for ventricular arrhythmia in patients with structural heart disease (2020).

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Use-dependent Na channel block selectively dampens high-frequency neuronal firing (epileptic foci) and reduces glutamate release; mood-stabilising mechanism less well-defined but likely involves glutamate normalisation in limbic circuits.

drug_interactions_pk.clinical_effect: Lamotrigine t1/2 ↑ to ~70 h; AUC ↑ 2× — major SJS risk factor; half all doses when combined.
Lamotrigine t1/2 ↓ to ~14 h; AUC ↓ 50% — double dose typically needed.
Lamotrigine clearance ↑ ~50% during active pill weeks; spikes during pill-free week.

pharmacogenetics.phenotype_effects: HLA-B*15:02 carriers (predominantly Han Chinese, SE Asian) have ~1000× higher SJS/TEN risk — pre-prescription testing recommended in these populations. HLA-A*31:01 also confers risk in European populations. UGT1A4*2/*3 alleles affect clearance.

tolerance_and_dependence.withdrawal_syndrome: Seizure rebound in epilepsy patients; mood instability in bipolar. Taper over ≥2 weeks recommended.

off_targets.clinical_consequence: Stevens-Johnson syndrome / toxic epidermal necrolysis in ~1/1000 (epilepsy) to ~1/2500 (bipolar). Slow titration (25 mg×2 wk, 50 mg×2 wk, then up to 100-200 mg) reduces risk roughly 10-fold. Risk amplified by valproate co-administration.
FDA 2020 warning: arrhythmia risk in patients with structural heart disease (Brugada-pattern ECG, conduction disease).

demographic_differences.sex: Women on combined oral contraceptives need ~50% higher doses during active pill weeks.
demographic_differences.renal_or_hepatic: Severe hepatic impairment: clearance ↓ 50%; severe renal impairment: caution with metabolite accumulation.

notes: The slow 6-week titration schedule is non-negotiable for safety, not gradual dose-finding — rapid titration is the dominant SJS/TEN risk factor independent of total dose.

name: Rimcazole

binding.tissue_or_cell: rat and guinea pig brain membranes
binding.notes: Ferris et al. 1986 — original characterisation. Selective sigma antagonist; ~100× weaker at PCP/NMDA site (IC50 43 μM). No significant μ/δ/κ opioid activity at 10 μM.
Rimcazole is unusual: blocks DAT without producing cocaine-like behavioural effects, possibly due to dual sigma antagonism. Inspired SAR programs for cocaine-abuse treatment.
Original antipsychotic mechanism could not be explained by direct D2 blockade (Ferris 1986); negligible postsynaptic dopaminergic effects in vivo.

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Sigma-1 antagonism may modulate dopaminergic neuronal firing indirectly; mechanism of antipsychotic action remains unclear and trials failed.

data_gaps_remaining: human PK data (no published clinical pharmacokinetic studies)
precise Ki for human sigma-1 vs sigma-2 subtypes
notes: Investigational atypical antipsychotic from Burroughs Wellcome that failed Phase III. Of historical interest because it was the first selective sigma antagonist trialed as an antipsychotic, ultimately disproving the sigma-receptor hypothesis of schizophrenia.

name: Befuraline

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Proposed dual mechanism: monoamine reuptake inhibition (NE/5-HT) plus phosphodiesterase inhibition; active metabolite benzylpiperazine (BZP) likely contributes via its own monoamine releasing activity.

data_gaps_remaining: receptor binding Ki values (not characterised at modern targets)
notes: Discontinued German antidepressant (1970s development) at oral 100-300 mg/d. Its major active metabolite benzylpiperazine (BZP) is now better known as a recreational stimulant and Schedule I drug in many jurisdictions — befuraline is essentially a BZP prodrug masked by the benzofuroyl carrier.

name: Medifoxamine

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Weak DAT inhibition (preferential) and even weaker SERT inhibition; 5-HT2A/2C antagonism. Drug not well-characterised at modern cloned receptors.

off_targets.clinical_consequence: Fulminant hepatitis cases led to withdrawal (Morocco 1999, France 2000). Mechanism likely reactive metabolite via diphenoxy moiety.

data_gaps_remaining: receptor binding Ki at modern targets
notes: Withdrawn 1999-2000 due to hepatotoxicity. No longer clinically available.

name: EXP-561

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Triple monoamine reuptake inhibitor (5-HT/NE/DA) without producing the chronic adaptive changes (β-adrenergic downregulation) seen with tricyclics — distinguishing pharmacological feature.

tolerance_and_dependence.receptor_downregulation_half_time: Notably failed to induce β-adrenergic downregulation typical of TCAs

data_gaps_remaining: any data more recent than 1970s preclinical work
notes: DuPont investigational SNDRI from 1960s-70s that failed clinical trials and was never marketed. Structurally a rigid bicyclic phenethylamine analog. Notable for being one of the earliest reported triple-reuptake inhibitors.

class_name: Prescription psychiatric drugs — SSRIs, SNRIs, atypical antidepressants, MAOIs, atypical antipsychotics, and mood stabilisers
shared_mechanism: These compounds split into mechanistically distinct subclasses despite their shared therapeutic indication. SSRIs selectively block the serotonin transporter (SERT) with Ki values typically <5 nM at cloned hSERT, raising synaptic 5-HT acutely and producing delayed (2-3 week) somatodendritic 5-HT1A autoreceptor desensitisation that gates the antidepressant response. Atypical antidepressants act through diverse mechanisms: mirtazapine via α2-autoreceptor + 5-HT2/3 antagonism (no transporter blockade), bupropion via NDRI. MAOIs irreversibly form covalent adducts on monoamine oxidase A and/or B, requiring 2-week enzyme resynthesis for washout; moclobemide uniquely is reversible (RIMA). Atypical antipsychotics are defined functionally by 5-HT2A:D2 receptor binding ratios above unity (clozapine ~30:1, olanzapine ~3:1) — the 5-HT2A blockade enhances cortical DA release while D2 blockade reduces mesolimbic DA, separating antipsychotic efficacy from extrapyramidal side-effects. Lithium uncompetitively inhibits GSK-3β by displacing Mg2+, depletes inositol via IMPase inhibition. Lamotrigine blocks voltage-gated sodium channels in a use- and state-dependent manner.
shared_pk_summary: CYP2D6 and CYP2C19 are the meta-axes for most antidepressant variability. Fluoxetine and paroxetine are mechanism-based CYP2D6 inhibitors AND substrates, producing severe nonlinear PK and persistent inhibition (weeks after stopping fluoxetine). Citalopram/escitalopram cleared by CYP2C19 — PMs require dose reduction. Sertraline goes mainly via CYP2B6/2C19. Fluvoxamine is the prototype CYP1A2 inhibitor (raises clozapine, theophylline, caffeine, melatonin levels). Antipsychotics divide by metabolism: olanzapine via UGT1A4 + CYP1A2 (smoking induces, fluvoxamine inhibits); clozapine via CYP1A2/2D6/3A4. Lamotrigine via UGT1A4 — valproate halves clearance, carbamazepine doubles it. Lithium and gabapentinoids are renally excreted unchanged with PK closely tied to GFR.
shared_safety: Five class-defining safety issues. (1) Serotonin syndrome from combining any 5-HT-elevating agent with an MAOI requires 2-5 week washout. (2) QTc prolongation: citalopram >40 mg (FDA black box), ziprasidone, methadone; mediated by hERG block by parent compound and DCT metabolite. (3) Metabolic syndrome from antipsychotics (olanzapine, clozapine highest) — driven by 5-HT2C + H1 + M3 antagonism causing weight gain and diabetogenic effects. (4) Stevens-Johnson syndrome with lamotrigine, especially with valproate co-administration or rapid titration — HLA-B*15:02 increases risk 1000× in Asian populations. (5) Tyramine 'cheese reaction' with irreversible MAOIs requires dietary restriction. SSRI discontinuation syndrome is dose-, t1/2-, and anticholinergic-load-dependent — paroxetine (short t1/2 + M1 block) is worst, fluoxetine (long-acting metabolite) is mildest. Pregnancy: paroxetine alone is category D for cardiac malformations; lithium for Ebstein anomaly (low absolute risk); valproate strongly teratogenic; sertraline/citalopram generally considered safest SSRIs in pregnancy. Lithium narrow therapeutic index (0.6-1.2 mM target) with toxicity ≥1.5 mM — NSAIDs/ACEis/thiazides reduce renal clearance and precipitate intoxication.
sar_summary: SSRI SAR is dominated by the orthosteric SERT pocket binding pose: fluoxetine's aryloxyalkylamine, sertraline's tetralin, paroxetine's piperidine, and citalopram's phthalan — each occupies the same site with different selectivities for off-targets driven by accessory pharmacophores (paroxetine's piperidine for NET, sertraline's dichloro substitution for DAT). Atypical antipsychotic SAR balances D2 affinity against 5-HT2A:D2 ratio (the higher the ratio, the more 'atypical'); clozapine's tricyclic dibenzodiazepine scaffold with N-methylpiperazine is the prototype, with thienobenzodiazepine (olanzapine) and dibenzothiazepine (quetiapine) being scaffold-conservative successors. Aripiprazole's dichlorophenylpiperazine + quinolinone is the unique partial-agonist scaffold. MAOI SAR turns on the warhead: hydrazine (phenelzine) reduces FAD non-selectively; cyclopropylamine (tranylcypromine) opens to form a covalent adduct; propargyl (selegiline, rasagiline) provides MAO-B selectivity. Lamotrigine's phenyltriazine is sui generis as a use-dependent Na blocker, distinct from the hydantoin (phenytoin) and dibenzazepine (carbamazepine) sodium-channel-blocking scaffolds.
